A '''Schnorr group''', proposed by [[Claus P. Schnorr]], is a large prime-order [[subgroup]] of <math>\mathbb{Z}_p^\times</math>, the [[multiplicative group of integers modulo n|multiplicative group of integers modulo <math>p</math>]] for some [[Prime number|prime]] <math>p</math>. <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schnorr |first1=C. P. |title=Efficient signature generation by smart cards |journal=Journal of Cryptology |date=1 January 1991 |volume=4 |issue=3 |pages=161–174 |doi=10.1007/BF00196725 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00196725 |access-date=25 July 2026 |language=en |issn=1432-1378}}</ref>

== Definition ==

To generate such a group, generate <math>p</math>, <math>q</math>, <math>r</math> such that

:<math>p = qr + 1</math>

with <math>p</math>, <math>q</math> prime. Then choose any <math>h</math> in the range <math>1 < h < p</math> until you find one such that

:<math>h^r \not\equiv 1\;(\text{mod}\;p)</math>.

This value

:<math>g = h^r\text{ mod }p</math>

is a generator of a subgroup of <math>\mathbb{Z}_p^\times</math> of order <math>q</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Singh |first1=Priyanka |last2=Khari |first2=Manju |last3=Kaundanya |first3=Nikhil S. |editor1-last=Bin Ahmad |editor1-first=Khairol Amali |editor2-last=Ahmad |editor2-first=Khaleel |editor3-last=Dulhare |editor3-first=Uma N. |title=Impact of Group Theory in Cryptosystem |journal=Functional Encryption |date=2021 |pages=19–36 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-60890-3_2 |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-60890-3_2 |access-date=25 July 2026 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Applications ==

Schnorr groups are useful in [[discrete log]] based [[cryptosystems]] including [[Schnorr signature]]s and [[Digital Signature Algorithm|DSA]]. In such applications, typically <math>p</math> is chosen to be large enough to resist [[index calculus]] and related methods of solving the discrete-log problem (perhaps 1024 to 3072 bits), while <math>q</math> is large enough to resist the [[birthday attack]] on discrete log problems, which works in any group (perhaps 160 to 256 bits).  Because the Schnorr group is of prime order, it has no non-trivial proper subgroups, thwarting [[Small subgroup confinement attack | confinement attacks]] due to small subgroups.  Implementations of protocols that use Schnorr groups must verify where appropriate that integers supplied by other parties are in fact members of the Schnorr group; <math>x</math> is a member of the group if <math>0 < x < p</math> and <math>x^q \equiv 1\;(\text{mod }p)</math>. Any member of the group except the element <math>1</math> is also a generator of the group.
